sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 12.8% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, rising from $4,860.4m to $14,342.9m [F1][F10][F198].
The path was a step change, not a smooth compound: revenue jumped 89.1% in FY2021 to $16,071.7m [F6][D241], then fell 24.3% in FY2022 to $12,172.9m [F7][D292].
REGEN-COV U.S. sales of $5,828.0m contributed 66.4pp of FY2021 growth [S48][D582], and those sales fell to zero in FY2022, a 36.3pp drag [S49][D585].
Since FY2022 revenue has grown only 5.6% a year to FY2025 [D767], and FY2025 growth was 1.0% [D440].
In FY2025 net product sales fell 17.3%, subtracting 9.3pp from growth [D506][D507], while collaboration revenue rose 21.0% and added 9.0pp [D522][D523].

U.S. EYLEA sales dropped 42.4% to $2,747.8m, a 14.2pp drag, on lower volumes from competitive pressure, compounded bevacizumab and the EYLEA HD transition, plus a lower net selling price [S43][D577][D578][P10].
EYLEA HD partly offset that, rising 36.3% to $1,636.9m and adding 3.1pp, on higher volumes partly offset by a lower net selling price [S64][D613][D614][P11].
Regeneron's share of Sanofi antibody profits grew 33.6% to $5,241.6m, adding 9.3pp, driven by higher Dupixent sales [S52][D591][D592][P9].
Operating costs grew 4.4pp faster than revenue in FY2025, at 5.4% [D464][D457], and operating income fell 10.3% against 1.0% revenue growth [D441][D440].
Operating margin of 24.9% in FY2025 is the window low, 9.7pp below the 34.6% median and 30.8pp below the 55.7% FY2021 high [F30][D749][D751][D750].
The FY2025 bridge was R&D -4.7pp, other lines -0.5pp, SG&A +2.0pp, for a net 3.2pp decline [D465][D467][D466][D453].
R&D rose 14.0% to $5,850.2m, or 40.8% of revenue [X34][D455][D420], and SG&A fell 8.6% to $2,700.0m primarily on lower charitable contributions to Good Days [X47][D456][P5].
In FY2025 net margin of 31.4% sat 6.5pp above the 24.9% operating margin [F50][F30], helped by $1,652.8m of other income [X117] and a 13.9% effective tax rate [D427].
Operating cash flow of $4,978.9m was 1.11x net income in FY2025 [F80][F40][D428], while free cash flow of $4,080.5m was 0.91x net income [F100][D429].
Free cash flow of $4,080.5m was a 28.4% margin [F100][D425], above the 26.4% window median [D757], with capex at 6.3% of revenue and 1.65x D&A [D424][D430].
Receivables fell 7.6% to $5,741.1m, and days sales outstanding were 146 [X197][D462][D438], while stock-based compensation of $993.7m was 20.0% of operating cash flow [X77][D431].
Net cash of $16,879.9m equals 117.7% of revenue [D434][D435], in the 100th percentile of eight biopharma peers against a -50.7% median [D780][D781].
Debt is a flat $1,985.9m [F187][D461], and the current ratio of 4.13x sits above the 3.97x window median [F180][D766].
Buybacks and dividends of $3,808.9m consumed 93.3% of free cash flow in FY2025 [D436][D437], and the diluted share count fell 5.6% [D459].
The balance sheet is the strongest part of the story, but the rising payout against free cash flow leaves less room if EYLEA erosion continues.
Operating margin has fallen four years running, from 55.7% in FY2021 to 24.9% in FY2025, a 30.7pp decline [F26][F30][R1].
The decline is driven by EYLEA erosion and rising R&D intensity, so the margin low is a structural mix shift rather than a one-year cost spike.
FY2018 and FY2019 revenue in the table is a later recast: $5,145.6m versus $6,710.8m first reported, and $6,557.6m versus $7,863.4m [F3][X3][F4][X4][R2].
Growth and margins spanning those recast years mix two presentations, so the FY2018-FY2019 comparisons should not anchor a trend conclusion.
Whether U.S. EYLEA sales fall below the FY2025 level of $2,747.8m [S43] will confirm or reverse the product decline, in the FY2026 10-K.
Whether operating margin holds above the FY2025 window low of 24.9% [D749] will show if the four-year slide has stopped, in the FY2026 10-K.
Whether R&D stays above the FY2025 level of 40.8% of revenue [D420] against the 34.6% median [D760] will indicate whether reinvestment keeps pressuring margin, in the FY2026 10-K.
